results.name: network_game_list_find_entry
results.evidence: Selects the 4-slot list (DAT_006b53d8/DAT_00719448) or 8-slot list (DAT_006b42d8/DAT_0071944c) by pointer identity of an incoming register arg, then scans 0x88-dword entries comparing a 4-dword key at entry+0x10 against param_1+0x20c..0x21c, returning the matching index or -1.
results.summary: Searches whichever of two fixed-size server-entry lists (history, max 4; favorites, max 8) is selected via a register pointer for an entry whose key fields match the caller's record, returning its index or -1.

results.name: network_game_list_add_entry
results.evidence: Same list-selection pattern as 0x4b5760 (DAT_006b53d8/DAT_00719448 max 4 vs DAT_006b42d8/DAT_0071944c max 8); if the selected list's count is below its max it copies a 0x88-dword entry into the next free slot and increments the count.
results.summary: Appends a 0x88-dword entry to whichever of the two server-entry lists is addressed by a register pointer, if that list has not reached its capacity (4 or 8), returning success.

results.name: network_game_list_remove_entry
results.evidence: Calls network_game_list_find_entry (0x4b5760) to locate the entry, then memmove()s the remaining 0x220-byte entries down over it and decrements the list's count global.
results.summary: Removes the entry matching the caller's key from whichever server-entry list is addressed by a register pointer, compacting the array and decrementing its count.

results.name: network_game_list_load
results.evidence: Zeroes both DAT_006b53d8 (max 4) and DAT_006b42d8 (max 8) arrays and their counts, then (if a profile-loaded flag in DAT_00714e7c is set) copies a set of default/system entries (DAT_006b1868, count DAT_006b1844) into the first list via network_game_list_add_entry, and copies up to 4 profile-stored entries (from a structure at offset 0x1108) directly into the same list, deduplicating via network_game_list_remove_entry.
results.summary: Resets the history/favorites server-entry lists and repopulates the history list from built-in defaults and the player's saved profile, removing any duplicate entries.

results.name: network_game_list_restore_matching_options
results.evidence: Copies the current ~8KB options block at DAT_00714e80 into a local buffer, calls FUN_0053b5a0/FUN_0053b2b0 (UI setup) and then for each of the DAT_00719448 history entries calls FUN_0053b470 to test a match, restoring the full options via FUN_0053b700 into the local buffer when found, before FUN_0053b620 closes out.
results.summary: Iterates the history server list looking for an entry matching the current game options and, on a match, restores the saved full option set for use by the network-game UI.

results.name: network_game_list_toggle_favorite
results.evidence: Uses FUN_004b5560 to resolve two UI list-box identities/id-arrays (4-slot and 8-slot, matching the history/favorites lists), locates param_1 in whichever list-box it belongs to, copies the corresponding 0x88-dword entry into the other list via network_game_list_add_entry, and calls network_game_list_remove_entry (0x4b5850) on the source; also updates linked widget selection fields afterward.
results.summary: Moves a selected server entry between the history and favorites lists (e.g. an "add/remove favorite" UI action), updating the affected list-box widgets.

results.name: video_resolution_compare
results.evidence: Passed as the comparator to _qsort over the DAT_006b6690 resolution table (stride 0x4c) in video_resolution_list_build (0x4bad40); compares the first dword (width) then the second dword (height) of each record.
results.summary: qsort comparator that orders two (width,height) resolution records ascending by width then by height.

results.name: video_refresh_rate_compare
results.evidence: Passed as the comparator to _qsort over each resolution's per-mode refresh-rate array in video_resolution_list_build (0x4bad40), sizeof element 4; compares two plain uint values.
results.prototype: unsigned int __cdecl video_refresh_rate_compare(unsigned int *a, unsigned int *b)
results.summary: qsort comparator that orders two refresh-rate values ascending.

results.name: video_display_modes_enumerate
results.evidence: Enumerates modes through a DirectDraw/Direct3D-style vtable (offsets 0x18/0x1c on DAT_0071d178), filters by colour depth (DAT_0069fe3c), available video memory (DAT_00722bb0), a "-vidmode" command-line override (string referenced, checked via __stricmp), and resolution/aspect limits, then calls video_resolution_add (0x4badc0) for each accepted mode.
results.summary: Enumerates the display device's supported video modes and, after filtering by memory, colour depth, command-line override and resolution/aspect limits, feeds each valid width/height/refresh combination into the resolution list builder.

results.name: video_resolution_list_build
results.evidence: Zeroes the DAT_006b6690 resolution table and DAT_007196cc count, calls video_display_modes_enumerate (0x4baba0) to populate it, sorts it with video_resolution_compare, then sorts each entry's refresh-rate sub-array with video_refresh_rate_compare.
results.summary: Rebuilds the sorted list of available screen resolutions and, for each, the sorted list of supported refresh rates.

results.name: video_resolution_add
results.evidence: Matches the naming hint (cea-pdb: video_resolution_add) and the code: dedups a (width,height) pair against DAT_006b6690/DAT_006b6694, formats its display name with FUN_00557930(L"%d x %d", ...), and inserts a refresh-rate value into that resolution's rate list (max 8) if not already present.
results.summary: Adds a width/height resolution entry to the video mode table (creating it if new) and records an associated refresh rate for it, up to 8 rates per resolution; width is passed on the stack, height in EAX, refresh rate on the stack.

results.name: video_refresh_rate_find_index
results.evidence: Bounds-checks a resolution index (in_ECX) against DAT_007196cc, then scans that resolution's DAT_006b66bc rate sub-array (length from DAT_006b66b8) for a value equal to an incoming register (unaff_EDI), returning its index or -1.
results.summary: Finds the index of a given refresh-rate value within a specific resolution's rate list, both passed in registers; returns -1 if not found.

results.name: video_options_menu_populate_from_settings
results.evidence: Walks a widget tree (child/sibling links at +0x34/+0x2c, type tag at +0xe==2) locating resolution/refresh, gamma, and several boolean/quality controls, and writes each control's value (widget+0x40/+0x12/+0x24) from fields of a settings struct at param_2 offsets 0xa68 (width), 0xa6a (height), 0xa6c (refresh), 0xa6f/0xa70/0xa71/0xa72/0xa73/0xa74 (quality/toggle bytes) and 0xa76 (gamma), also matching the resolution against the video_resolution_add table and calling chimera__gamma to apply gamma changes.
results.summary: Populates the video-options menu's widgets (resolution, refresh rate, gamma, and several quality/toggle controls) from a video settings structure, disabling controls the current hardware/driver does not support.

results.name: video_options_menu_open
results.evidence: Calls FUN_0053b000 to fetch the current video/game options into a stack buffer, and on success passes them to video_options_menu_populate_from_settings (0x4baec0) before calling widget_play_sound_effect.
results.summary: Handles opening the video options menu: fetches the current settings and populates the menu's widgets from them, playing the UI open sound on success.

results.name: video_options_menu_update
results.evidence: Matches the naming hint (cea-pdb: video_menu_update) and the code: reformats the resolution label from the video_resolution_add table, formats the selected refresh rate with FUN_00557930(L"%d Hz", ...), nudges a gamma value up/down based on a widget direction field and calls chimera__gamma to apply it, then calls FUN_004a66b0.
results.summary: Updates the video options menu after the user changes a control: refreshes the resolution/refresh-rate display text and adjusts and applies the gamma setting.

results.name: command_line_process_connect
results.evidence: References the strings "-connect", "-name", and "-password" and calls FUN_00542760 (command-line argument lookup) plus player_profile_load and a wcscmp; Ghidra removed most of the branch logic as unreachable, leaving only the "-connect" lookup visible.
results.summary: Checks the command line for a "-connect" (with associated "-name"/"-password") launch argument to auto-join a multiplayer server at startup.
